issues.summary: The empty-tag guard can essentially never trigger, because a 'released' event always carries a tag_name.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:290 only runs the job when action == 'released', and GitHub requires a tag for every release, so the `-z` check at :301-305 is effectively dead. It is harmless belt-and-braces that matches the PR's stated goal of never pushing an empty tag, so the concrete cost is nil.

issues.summary: 'Validate release tag' only checks for an empty value, not that the tag is a valid Docker tag.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:301-305 tests only `-z "$RELEASE_TAG"`. A git tag containing '/' or '+' would pass this check and then fail in build-push-action at :318-319. Release tags here are in practice semver-like, so this is a minor gap and a name/behaviour mismatch.

issues.summary: Every release pushes ':latest', so a patch release on an older line moves latest backwards.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:320 always tags `:latest` on any released event. This is real, but the behaviour predates the PR and that line is unchanged, so it is out of scope and at most low.

issues.summary: The concurrency group uses github.ref rather than the release payload.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:21. On release events github.ref is refs/tags/<tag>, so the grouping works. The finding itself concedes it is likely fine, and there is no defect.

issues.summary: No comment explains why release.tag_name replaces github.ref_name.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:294-295 adds RELEASE_TAG with no inline rationale, while the file comments other choices (:6-9, :262-267). The rationale is in the PR description, so the missing comment is a documentation preference with little concrete cost.

issues.summary: The staging job still uses github.ref_name with no comment explaining the difference.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:284 runs only on push to main, where ref_name is reliably 'main'. The difference is natural given the event type and needs no change.

issues.summary: The validation step runs after checkout rather than before it.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:296-305: checkout comes before the validation step. Moving validation first would save only a few seconds in a case that practically never happens.
